name: Bimetric-Chronos: MOND-dynamics in a Timelike-Sector Metric, GR-Lensing in a Spatial-Sector Metric
claimed_mechanism: We fundamentally decouple the MONDian acceleration dynamics from the lensing carrier by splitting the gravitational field into two distinct metrics: h_mu_nu (the kinematic/timelike sector) and g_mu_nu (the spatial/lensing sector). The MOND dynamics (and its associated preferred-frame response) are entirely localized in h_mu_nu, where the e^-y screening suppresses its PPN-visible kinetic terms. Meanwhile, the lensing carrier (the spatial metric g_mu_nu) carries a pure GR kinetic structure, entirely immune to the e^-y suppression. This cleanly satisfies P7 because the kinetic normalization of the propagating lensing mode is independent of the screened MOND sector.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the spatial metric g_mu_nu exactly reproduces GR lensing (giving the required massless scalar + tensor response for Phi=Psi). The MONDian acceleration dynamics emerge from h_mu_nu, which modifies the time-time and spatial curvature potentials to produce the expected mu(y) scaling of the acceleration. Because the preferred-frame couplings in h_mu_nu are screened by e^-y, the Solar System sees a vanishing PPN alpha_2, while the unscreened spatial metric perfectly handles the lensing escape of DC-001.
inequivalence_argument: This is structurally inequivalent to DC-001 (local frameless lensing) because it explicitly includes a timelike preferred-frame vector (u_mu) in the h_mu_nu sector, breaking the no-preferred-frame condition that causes DC-001's under-lensing. It is inequivalent to DC-002 (AeST) because the standard kinetic vector (u_mu) does NOT source the lensing carrier; the lensing carrier is g_mu_nu, which has an independent GR kinetic normalization and is not a stiff 6-DOF aether tied to a constant K_B coupling. It is inequivalent to DC-010 (khronometric) because the MOND screening does NOT zero out the kinetic term of the propagating lensing mode (g_mu_nu), avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wall.
